title: Cuba Is Not Venezuela or Jamaica
author: Riva Enteen
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Screen-
Shot-2026-08-12-at-9.50.15-AM-680x462.png)

Image by Mauro Lima.

Veteran Intelligence Professionals for Sanity (VIPS) recently issued a memo
which states: [Cuba is not
Venezuela.](https://consortiumnews.com/2026/05/29/vips-memo-avoiding-
catastrophic-failure-in-cuba/) What does that mean? “The same people who keep
’57 Chevrolets on the road with a coat hanger will wreak havoc against a
foreign-imposed regime.”

In 1975, Jamaica’s socialist Prime Minister Michael Manley expressed support
for Cuba’s solidarity with the Angola liberation struggle.

He later described [Henry Kissinger’s
response](https://www.tenementyaadmedia.com/kissingerja-transcript-1-1-1):
“Suddenly he [Kissinger] raised the question of Angola and said he would
appreciate it if Jamaica would at least remain neutral on the subject of the
Cuban army presence in Angola. I told him that I could make no promises but
would pay the utmost attention to his request…and that before taking any
official position on it internationally, I would communicate with him in
Washington. Afterwards Kissinger…brought up…the Jamaican proposal for the
hundred million dollar trade credit…I had the feeling he was sending a
message.”

“We took the Angolan situation seriously. We knew what Jamaica’s duty must be.
Within five days of his leaving, I let Kissinger know that Jamaica had decided
to support the Cuban army presence in Angola because we were satisfied that
they were there because of the South African invasion. The Jamaican government
then publicly announced its support for Cuba in Angola. I never heard another
word about the hundred million dollar trade credit. Soon after the news that
Jamaica was supporting Cuba, Kissinger confidante, James Reston of _The New
York Times_ , wrote a vicious and utterly inaccurate article about
Jamaica….This started a chain reaction in the US press which never ceased
until we were finally defeated in the elections of October 1980.”

The days of Michael Manley’s support of Cuba are long gone, but recently,
current Jamaica Prime Minister Andrew Holness [expressed concern for the
humanitarian crisis in Cuba](https://www.miamiherald.com/news/nation-
world/world/americas/article314849622.html). As a result, soon thereafter, the
U.S. directed Jamaica to end its five-decade program with Cuba to provide
doctors and other health-care workers to Jamaica’s poor, and Jamaica complied.
Sovereignty means the power of a country to control its own government. If
Jamaica needed to comply, is it sovereign?

Has Venezuela compromised its sovereignty? Kit Klarenberg recently published
[The White Helmets Invade Venezuela](https://www.kitklarenberg.com/p/the-
white-helmets-invade-venezuela?hide_intro_popup=true), which states that on
June 27th, a “specialized” team of “highly trained search and rescue
specialists” flew into Venezuela from Damascus.

Syrian head-chopper/leader Ahmad al-Sharaa ordered the group to assist
disaster efforts in response to Venezuela’s devastating twin earthquakes.
“Among them are members of the notorious White Helmets. A bogus humanitarian
group constructed by MI6, they played a central role in Britain’s protracted
coup of Bashar Assad. Are the White Helmets similarly in Venezuela to assist
regime change?”

It is stark irony that the White Helmets’ expertise in dealing with complex
rubble and the extraction of trapped survivors thanks to the [West’s dirty
war](https://www.kitklarenberg.com/p/syrian-dirty-wars-secret-origins) against
Assad, will be used to participate in international emergency response
missions, “with Venezuela being their debut,” states Klarenberg.

He continues: “The White Helmets will ‘work in close coordination’ with
international rescue units in shattered Caracas for up to 10 days, ‘with the
possibility of extending the mission depending on operational requirements and
developments on the ground.’ An ‘operational requirement’ of the rescuers may
be assisting in the construction of quasi-state structures in Venezuela, a la
Syria, ensuring Western powers have the requisite people, organisations and
structures in place locally to take over when the embattled interim government
of Delcy Rodríguez finally collapses.”

There is still a dispute about reports in the [ _Miami
Herald_](https://www.theburningplatform.com/2026/01/05/major-questions-
finally-answered-about-trumps-venezuelan-adventure/) that former Venezuelan
Vice President Delcy Rodríguez, now Acting President with the approval of the
U.S., had reached out to Washington to present a “more acceptable” alternative
to the Maduro regime before his kidnapping in January. [ _The
Telegraph_](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2026/01/04/secret-meetings-
point-to-inside-job-to-take-down-maduro/) quotes Francisco Santos Calderón,
Colombia’s former vice president of eight years: “I’m absolutely certain Delcy
Rodríguez handed [Maduro] over. All the information we have, you start to put
it together and say: ‘Oh, this was an operation in which they handed him
over…’ They didn’t remove him. They handed him over.”

Regardless of whether Rodríguez explicitly cooperated with the plot to remove
Maduro, these facts are not in dispute: After Maduro and his wife were
kidnapped, Trump threatened, “If she [Rodríguez] doesn’t do what’s right, she
is going to pay a very big price, probably bigger than Maduro.” It appears she
did what Trump declared was “right.”

[According to  _Venezuela Analysis_ ,](https://venezuelanalysis.com/news/us-
conducts-extrajudicial-execution-in-venezuela-thanks-rodriguez-for-support/)
since Maduro’s abduction, Rodríguez has fast-tracked a diplomatic
rapprochement with the U.S., and reformed oil and mining legislation to favor
Western investment. The U.S. continues to [dictate conditions on Venezuela’s
energy industry](https://venezuelanalysis.com/news/trump-administration-
extracts-renewed-venezuela-oil-concessions-as-rodriguez-touts-new-deals/) for
the benefit of U.S. and Western corporations and issued multiple [sanctions
waivers to allow Western corporations to secure favorable energy and mining
agreements](https://venezuelanalysis.com/news/venezuela-earthquake-death-toll-
rises-us-southcom-deploys-military-assets/).

The U.S. seized control of Venezuelan export revenues, disbursing a portion
back to Caracas at U.S. officials’ discretion. Transactions between Caracas
and its allies China, Russia, Cuba and Iran are prohibited by the waivers and
subject to secondary sanctions. The U.S. demands “ending oil shipments to
Cuba, halting cocaine trafficking routes [allowing extrajudicial murder on the
open seas (Ed.)], curbing Iranian and Russian access, and opening Venezuela’s
energy sector to U.S. companies…”

Trump then declared, “Because of this cooperation, I have [cancelled the
previously expected second Wave of
Attacks](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1/9/trump-cancels-second-wave-of-
attacks-on-venezuela-after-cooperation)…however, all ships will stay ‌in place
for safety and security purposes.” The U.S. then lifted sanctions on Rodríguez
herself and, in April, the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced it would
issue new licenses to allow transactions with certain Venezuelan banks and
individuals.

_The Grayzone_ recently published a scathing piece entitled “[Delcy’s
‘gatekeeper’: sources say ex-Trump official Claver-Carone holds keys to
Caracas.” ](https://thegrayzone.com/2026/05/25/delcys-gatekeeper-trump-
caracas/)The article noted that, according to an insider who enjoys close
contacts within both the Venezuelan and U.S. governments, Marco Rubio’s
influence over Rodríguez is said to be “traced to one ‘gatekeeper’: former
Trump Latin America envoy Mauricio Claver-Carone. ‘Mauricio is picking who can
operate and Delcy [Rodríguez] is taking instructions. Now he’s got a lock on
everything…He could say to anyone who wants to work in Venezuela, I’m the guy.
I have the keys. If you want to play ball, invest with me,” the source told
_The Grayzone_.

A former senior U.S. official with access to leadership in both Caracas and
Washington offered the same assessment, remarking to  _The Grayzone_ ,
“Mauricio’s calling the shots on private sector economic positions, and if
anyone wants in, they have to go to him.”

When the Trump administration announced that Venezuela could hire a financial
adviser to assist with its sovereign debt, Rodríguez initially planned a
public bidding process for the coveted post, but Claver-Carone ultimately
chose the person.

_Consortium News_ reported that Trump announced, “[We are going to run the
country](https://consortiumnews.com/2026/01/05/did-venezuela-vp-hand-over-
maduro-in-deal-with-the-us/) until such time as we can see a proper and
judicious transition. We can’t take a chance that someone else takes over
Venezuela who doesn’t have the good of the Venezuelan people in mind.”

If Trump were truly concerned about the Venezuelan people, he would end the
sanctions to facilitate disaster relief. But to add insult to injury, even
after the double earthquakes, Washington is [maintaining its punishing
economic sanctions](https://venezuelanalysis.com/news/venezuela-earthquake-
death-toll-rises-us-southcom-deploys-military-assets/) against Venezuela.

The U.S. Treasury Department issued a general license to authorize
transactions related to earthquake relief efforts, but Venezuelan assets
abroad, including bank accounts, remain frozen, so aid efforts still face
hurdles or require U.S. approval.

Caracas has also been unable to access some $4.8 billion in gold held by the
Bank of England, as well as nearly $5 billion in IMF Special Drawing Rights.

_CodePink_ states: “Too often, we’ve seen the U.S. and other Western countries
exploit natural disasters like this in order to deepen foreign control. In
Haiti, the U.S. and its allies have repeatedly pushed militarization and
politically conditioned aid instead of genuine recovery led by the country
itself…The world must refuse to allow Venezuela to be forced down the same
path.”

So not only is Venezuela unable to exercise its sovereign rights as a country,
but its capitulation to Uncle Sam has not even resulted in true assistance
with this national tragedy. Regime change is never for the benefit of the
country targeted, but only for U.S. financial and hegemonic interests. When
choreographed from outside the target country, regime change is an attack on
sovereignty.

To add further insult to injury,  _Venezuela Analysis_ reports that the
[Venezuelan government has welcomed an official Israeli
delegation](https://venezuelanalysis.com/news/venezuelan-govt-welcomes-
israeli-diplomatic-and-military-mission/) for hurricane relief, in the first
significant bilateral engagement since former President Hugo Chávez severed
ties with Israel in 2009.

Chávez fiercely denounced Operation Cast Lead as “genocide” and voiced
solidarity with the Palestinian people. Maduro maintained Chávez’s policy
position condemning Israeli military occupation and war crimes in Gaza and
Lebanon, as well as the June 2025 Twelve-Day War against Iran.

The Maduro government publicly
[endorsed](https://venezuelanalysis.com/news/venezuela-backs-south-africas-
icj-genocide-case-against-israel/) South Africa’s activation of the Genocide
Convention against Israel at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in 2024.

The arrival of an Israeli mission has drawn backlash from the Chavista
grassroots. Hindu Anderi, spokesperson for the Platform of Solidarity with the
Palestinian Cause, slammed the “hypocrisy” of Israel claiming the mantle of
humanitarianism amid its ongoing genocides in Gaza and Lebanon.

According to Anderi, “the Zionist regime wants to whitewash its record through
rescue teams…after condemning the Palestinian people to rubble.” Was Rodríguez
free to say no? If not, is Venezuela sovereign?

The proposed merger of the U.S. and Israeli militaries raises the question of
sovereignty as well. Dennis and Elizabeth Kucinich recently condemned
Congress’s plans in the 2027 NDAA to deepen U.S. strategic integration with
Israel as a plan to [surrender
sovereignty](https://consortiumnews.com/2026/06/29/for-the-250th-us-congress-
plans-to-surrender-
sovereignty/?eType=EmailBlastContent&eId=fe8684a9-2ed8-49ec-
bac7-0944aaf6e723).

[Section
224](https://armedservices.house.gov/uploadedfiles/fy27_ndaa_chairmans_mark_-
_final.pdf) of the House Armed Services Committee chairman’s mark for the FY27
NDAA would expand cooperation in defense research, development, testing,
evaluation, production and sustainment. The proposal goes beyond traditional
foreign military sales and existing cooperative programs by encouraging closer
collaboration among government agencies, defense contractors, research
institutions and technology developers from both countries.

After the House narrowly passed the bill, Thomas Massie (R-KY) said “Let’s
hope this version fails in the Senate because Section 2019 is a betrayal of
our sovereignty.”

With a large majority of Americans opposed to Israel’s daily acts of genocide,
why would Congress propose such a military partnership? Because of the
astronomical congressional contributions from AIPAC, some say Congress is
Israeli-occupied territory. If the U.S. puts Israel first, and not its own
interests, is the U.S. sovereign? Whose interests are shaping foreign policy?
The Epstein Syndicate?

Cuba is one of the few challengers to U.S. hegemony still standing. The U.S.
has waged a bipartisan war against Cuba for the [“sin” of reclaiming national
sovereignty](https://consortiumnews.com/2026/05/18/the-united-states-long-war-
on-cuba/), punishing Cuba for its defiance.

Eric Ross, a Ph.D. candidate in the History Department of the University of
Massachusetts, Amherst, asserts that “Despite this long war against Cuba, the
Cuban government and people have not abandoned their revolutionary project.
They have continued to build
[socialism](https://www.commondreams.org/tag/socialism) and a new social order
toward what Che Guevara described as the construction of “[new
[people]](https://www.marxists.org/archive/guevara/1965/03/man-
socialism.htm)”: human beings whose motivations, commitments and social
relations are not governed by opportunistic self-interest at the expense of
others, but by [solidarity](https://www.commondreams.org/tag/solidarity) and a
shared sense of collective humanity.”

Ross continued: “For more than six decades then, Cuba has represented the
‘[threat](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/01/addressing-
threats-to-the-united-states-by-the-government-of-cuba/)’ of example: the
possibility of building a more just and humane society in which the state
serves the people and not the other way around…[Since
1959](https://mises.org/mises-wire/brief-history-enduring-american-embargo-
against-cuba), Washington has pursued a singular, near-fanatical
[obsession](https://theconversation.com/why-is-the-us-so-obsessed-with-
controlling-cuba-280729) with reversing the [Cuban
Revolution](https://www.britannica.com/event/Cuban-Revolution) and restoring
the neocolonial shackles it once imposed on the island. Its aim has been not
only to undermine Cuba’s social transformation and internationalist
commitments, but to extinguish the example the revolution represented: that an
alternative to [U.S. hegemony](https://mronline.org/2023/07/20/200-years-of-
the-monroe-doctrine/) and capitalist underdevelopment was possible.”

Recently, CIA Director John Ratcliffe went to Havana to demand economic
“reforms” and the closing of Russian and Chinese listening posts in exchange
for U.S. assistance after Cuba declared its fuel reserves had run out. Cuba
has not succumbed.

Instead, the Cuban people have [vowed to
resist](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/4/10/cuban-president-defiant-
despite-trump-pressure-to-resign) a new U.S. invasion. The small island of
Cuba, with its indefatigable, courageous and compassionate people, will never
succumb to threats and give up their sovereignty.

Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel said Cuba is a “free sovereign state” with
the right to “self-determination,” and it is not “subject to the designs of
the United States.” Apparently, Cuba is not Venezuela. Cuba would rather go
down fighting.

Magazine](https://covertactionmagazine.com/author/rivaenteen/)._
